narrative.overview:
Church Presenter is the room behind the room. The sanctuary is dim, the service is happening, and the operator's screen must glow just enough to work by without spilling light or attention. Everything sits on a warm, brown-tinted near-black, and frosted panels float a layer above it. Light is spent only where hands and eyes are needed: Brass Fader Amber on the one action that matters, Live Green on the slide the congregation is seeing, and nothing else competing.

The system is dense, like a mixing console, but never cramped. Labels are small and uppercase, controls are compact, and the canvas or current-output frame is always the largest, brightest thing on screen. A serif display face (Iowan Old Style) gives the headings a reverent, printed-page voice. The system sans carries every control, so the tool still reads as precise software.

Controls are quiet until needed. Ghost and outlined buttons recede into the surface. Only the primary amber action and the live state carry visual weight, so a volunteer can find "what do I press next" at a glance.
keyCharacteristics: Warm dark base (Sanctuary Dark) with translucent frosted panels layered above it.
One accent voice: Brass Fader Amber for action, icons, and focus.
Three reserved state colors: green means live, violet means selected, red means destructive.
Serif display headings over a system-sans operator interface.
Dense, console-like spacing on a 4px rhythm. The 16:9 canvas is always the focal point.

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: Never hand-type an `rgba()` of an existing family. Use `rgb(var(--family-rgb) / alpha)`. Only shadow black, highlight white, button gradient stops and slide background art stay literal.

rules.name: The Green Means Live Rule
rules.body: Live Green appears only on the slide, output, or chip that is on the audience screen at this moment. Selected, saved, success, and "ready" states use amber or violet. Green is always paired with a visible "LIVE" label or dot, never color alone.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Brass Fader Amber is the only accent that asks for action. A screen has one filled amber button at most. Every other action is secondary, ghost, or a text link.

rules.name: The No Pure White Rule
rules.body: Text tops out at warm off-white (`text`). Pure `#fff` is reserved for slide content rendered on the audience canvas.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: No operator-facing text is smaller than 11px. The booth is dim, and the screen is often a laptop across a desk. Slide content on the canvas is exempt because it scales with the canvas.

rules.name: The Steady Digits Rule
rules.body: Clocks, timers, slide positions, and counts use tabular numerals so they don't shift while live.

rules.name: The Canvas Is the Center Rule
rules.body: In the editor and in live mode, the 16:9 slide is the largest element on screen at every width. Panels give up space before the canvas does.

rules.name: The Reflow, Never Hide Rule
rules.body: Narrow widths move panels; they never remove a feature. The inspector, rundown, next slide, and history must be reachable at every size.

rules.name: The Ambient Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft and offset downward. No hard offset shadows and no colored halos, except the amber lift on the primary button and the live glow on the output frame.

rules.name: The Seven Corners Rule
rules.body: Use a `--rounded-*` step, never a raw pixel radius. Slide content on the canvas is exempt because it scales with the canvas.

dos: **Do** keep Live Green exclusively for audience-visible state, always with a "LIVE" word or dot.
**Do** use Selection Violet for selected or editing state: rundown row, canvas element, active tab.
**Do** limit each view to one filled amber button. Make everything else secondary, ghost, or a link.
**Do** set screen titles, service names, dialog titles, and panel titles in the serif. Set everything interactive in the system sans.
**Do** keep operator text at 11px or larger, and use tabular numerals for anything that counts or ticks.
**Do** use warm off-white hairlines (8–15% opacity) for borders and the 9px / 14px radius pair for controls and panels.
**Do** reflow panels at narrow widths. The canvas stays the largest thing on screen.
**Do** respect the Reduce Transparency and Reduce Motion settings. Both must keep working.
donts: **Don't** use green for success toasts, "saved" states, or selection.
**Don't** use pure white UI text, solid grey borders, or a light theme surface.
**Don't** leave native grey form controls. Every select and input takes the recessed dark field style.
**Don't** add hard offset shadows or colored glows beyond the amber lift and the live frame glow.
**Don't** hide the inspector, rundown, next slide, or history at small widths. Move them instead.
**Don't** set operator UI text below 11px, and don't put a second framed focus box inside an already-framed field.
